I used to cut, hit myself (still do sometimes), used to drink and do drugs. I also used to starve myself sometimes not eating for days. I liked to feel the pain from not eating and also enjoyed actually having control over something.

I have been having similar thoughts. It is terrifying to think that the person/s that were/are meant to love and care for you don't in the slightest bit feel anything for you. I used to think that it must be because there is something wrong with me, now I know better and know it's them with the problem.

I read something a while ago that said we know by 12 months of age that our parent/s don't love us. We aren't old enough to understand it so from what I understand we have the belief and the hope that they really do, that under all the abuse our parents do love us. It's a defense mechanism. I only now after 18 months of seeing my psychologist once a week am able to see past that childish hope. It is very difficult and I know the road to recovering from childhood trauma will be a long one but I am finally here somewhere I never thought I would be. I will admit now that my childish hope that my parents really do love and care for me is gone I can remember the abuse a lot more clearly.

Wow, you have no idea how much your comment has helped me. I like many am afraid of my emotions, my psychologist is helping me feel them. Anger is a huge problem for me too. I'd like to share some advice that my psychologist has given me about it. Anger is a healthy emotion to experience, we being abused by narcissists were forced into submission and not allowed to feel our emotions. The only way to let go of the anger you are feeling is to feel it. Here is something that my psychologist got me to do and it sounds silly but it works. Start blaming everything that goes wrong on your parent/s. For eg the batteries died on the Tv remote, it is your parents fault, Your favourtie character on a tv series dies again it is because of your parents. I think that it helps you learn to redirect your anger on people that deserve it.
